title: Prayer for peace and unbroken bond
english: But the God of peace, in his love for humankind, will act with us so that Satan is crushed under the feet of us Christians, and every wicked pretext is driven away, so that the bond of Christ's unfeigned love, peace, right faith, and truth is not torn from us.

added_allusions.reason: The Greek 'the God of peace' with Satan crushed under our feet closely echoes Romans 16:20, the one verse joining all three elements.

translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.
baehrens: PG Epistula ad Joannem Hierosolymitanum u01-rem-early
orientation: Epiphanius, having just quoted Scripture against grumbling, now prays that God will crush Satan and preserve the bond of love, peace, faith, and truth among Christians.

title: Tearing the painted curtain at Anautha
english: But I heard that some grumbled against us. While we were traveling on to the holy place at Bethel to meet with your honor, we came to the village called Anautha. I saw a lamp burning, and when I asked I learned that there was a church in that place. I went in to pray, and I found a dyed curtain on the door, painted with some human image, idol-like. They said it was perhaps a likeness of Christ or of one of the saints, for I myself, though I saw it, do not remember whose image it was.

Knowing that it is an abomination for such things to be in a church, I tore it and advised wrapping a poor dead person in it. But those who grumbled said, “He ought to have replaced the curtain from his own means before he tore it,” although I had promised to send another in its place. I was slow to send it because pressing need held me.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.
baehrens: PG Epistula ad Joannem Hierosolymitanum u01-rem-mid
orientation: Epiphanius tells John what happened when he entered a church at Anautha while traveling to meet John at Bethel.

title: Sending the replacement curtain and urging John to prevent such hangings
english: I had expected to send one from Cyprus, but now I have sent what I found. Deign, then, to order the presbyter of the parish to receive what has been sent from the reader, and I ask you to command that such things not be hung in the churches. For it is fitting for your honor to care about all things and to examine carefully what is beneficial for the church of God and for the people entrusted to you.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.
baehrens: PG Epistula ad Joannem Hierosolymitanum u01-rem-close
orientation: Epiphanius is closing his letter to John of Jerusalem, explaining that he has now sent the replacement curtain and asking John to order the local presbyter to receive it and to prevent such images in churches.
